Featuring Brady Seals (cousin of Jim Seals and former member of Little Texas) and Lua Crofts (daughter of Dash Crofts), this dynamic duo brings a fresh and soulful interpretation of the original hits that defined a generation. With voices that echo their legendary family ties and a chemistry that captivates audiences of all ages, Seals & Crofts 2 perform beloved classics like “Summer Breeze,” “Diamond Girl,” and “We May Never Pass This Way (Again),” alongside new original music that honors the spirit and sincerity of the originals. More than just a tribute, Seals & Crofts 2 is a celebration of musical heritage, connection, and the enduring power of melody. Don’t miss this enchanting evening filled with nostalgia, harmony, and artistry that bridges generations. item.title: Jan 29, 2027 — Reed Timmer at American Music Theatre
item.description:
Events: Jan 29, 2027

Location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Highway East, Lancaster, PA, 17602

Price: Not supplied by this calendar; check event details

Dominate the Storm: A Heart Pumping Evening with Reed Timmer, America’s Most Famous Storm Chaser Never Stop Chasing! Experience the raw power of nature through the eyes of Dr. Reed Timmer, extreme meteorologist, scientist, and one of the world’s most renowned storm chasers. With a PhD in meteorology from the University of Oklahoma, Reed has devoted his life to intercepting the planet’s most dangerous storms, collecting groundbreaking scientific data, and helping audiences better understand how severe weather is changing. Over the past several decades, Reed has intercepted more than 1,000 tornadoes and 50 hurricanes, including EF5 tornadoes and Category 5 hurricanes. He is also the inventor of the Dominators – armored, tank-like storm-chasing vehicles equipped with advanced meteorological sensors, hydraulic anchoring spikes, drones, probes, balloons, and even model rockets. Since 2020, Reed has driven Dominator 3 directly into 10 tornadoes, more than any other person in history. His unforgettable expeditions include recording 140 mph winds from inside a Nebraska tornado and launching a trackable sensor into a mile-wide EF4 tornado in Kansas. Carried as high as 39,000 feet and reaching speeds of 190 mph, the sensor captured unprecedented data throughout its 30-mile journey inside the vortex. Currently chasing storms for the National Geographic Channel and RadarOmega, Reed also provides vital real-time reports through traditional and social media. Hear the incredible stories, witness breathtaking footage, and discover the science behind Earth’s most powerful storms during this heart-pumping live event. For Reed Timmer, “Never Stop Chasing” is more than a motto – it is a way of life. Subsequent iterations build on one another, but always yield something new that reflects what has come before. By undergoing this recursive process, Kent’s photographic iterations capture both rural and urban landscapes, visually documenting the passage of time.
